ORDER AND CERTIFICATE 
The above-captioned matter comes before the State Corporation Commission of the State 
of Kansas (Commission) for consideration and decision. Having examined its files and records, 
and being duly advised in the premises, the Commission makes the following findings: 
1. 
In its Order of April 30, 1984 in Docket No. 127,140-U, the Commission found 
that resellers were public utilities and subject to Commission regulation. As part of that 
regulation, the Commission directed resellers of telecommunications services to file applications 
for Certificates of Convenience and Authority and accompanying tariffs for approval. 
2. 
In its Order of March 21, 1994 in Docket No. 187,168-U, the Commission 
adopted revised streamlined rules and regulations governing resellers and interexchange carriers, 
designed to reflect changes occurring in the marketplace. 
3. 
On May 13, 2005, Comcast Phone of Kansas, L.L.C. (Comcast) filed the above- 
captioned application for a Certificate of Convenience and Authority to engage in the business of 
an interexchange services provider throughout the State of Kansas. Comcast proposes to provide 
interexchange long distance services to residential and business customers. 

4. 
On June 9, 2005, Commission staff (Staff) filed a memorandum recommending 
that the Commission grant Comcast's application. Staff suggested that Comcast be advised that 
it may not provide these services until a tariff has been filed with and approved by the 
Commission. 
5. 
Comcast is a Pennsylvania incorporated company properly registered with the 
office of the Kansas Secretary of State as a foreign corporation authorized to engage in business 
in Kansas and has an "active and in good standing" status with the Secretary's office. 
6. 
To the extent that Comcast's presence in Kansas would increase consumers' 
options for intrastate long distance services, Staff believes the general public would benefit from 
Commission approval of this application. 
7. 
The Commission finds and concludes that the public convenience will be 
promoted by increased options for interexchange long distance services by granting Comcast 
Phone of Kansas, L.L.C.'s application. The Commission, therefore, finds and concludes that 
Comcast Phone of Kansas, L.L.C. should be granted the authority requested in this docket. 
Comcast Phone of Kansas, L.L.C. should be advised that prior to providing service, a tariff must 
be filed with and approved by the Commission. 
IT IS, THEREFORE, BY THE COMMISSION ORDERED AND CERTIFIED THAT: 
A. 
The application of Comcast Phone of Kansas, L.L.C. for a Certificate of 
Convenience and Authority to transact business as a provider of interexchange 
telecommunications services within the State of Kansas is hereby granted pursuant to K.S.A. 66-
131, as set out in the above order. 
B. 
Prior to providing service, a tariff from Comcast Phone of Kansas, L.L.C. must be 
filed with and approved by the Commission. In addition, Comcast Phone of Kansas, L.L.C. is 

hereby reminded of its ongoing obligation to provide telephone relay services to its customers 
under the terms and conditions set forth in this order and under Kansas law. 
C. 
The parties have fifteen days, plus three days if service of this order is by mail, 
from the date this order was served in which to petition the Commission for reconsideration of 
any issue or issues decided herein. K.S.A. 66-118; K.S.A. 2004 Supp. 77-529(a)(l). 
D. 
The Commission retains jurisdiction over the subject matter and the parties for the 
purpose of entering such further order, or orders, as it may deem necessary. 
BY THE COMMISSION IT IS SO ORDERED AND CERTIFIED. 
Moline, Chr.; Krehbiel, Corn.; Moffet, Corn.
